title: Stabilize execution-path flapping during capacity surges — guardrails and eval harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-18 we observed repeated execution-path flapping across a subset of inference workers. The symptom was rapid kernel/route switching at microbatch boundaries which amplified per-request p95/p99 and caused increases in latency-sensitive client errors and retries. This ticket captures follow-up engineering work: hardened guardrails in the scheduler, sticky-path scoring TTL, probe damping, and an eval harness that reproduces surge-induced flapping in CI.
timeline: 2026-02-18 02:13 UTC — Detection: Automated SLO alerts (p99 latency and error spike) fired for regional pool eu-west-1-r1.
2026-02-18 02:17 UTC — Triage: On-call identified oscillation in kernel assignment logs; microbatch boundary churn and KV cache warmup thrash.
2026-02-18 02:45 UTC — Mitigation: Emergency knob applied to disable speculative kernel probing on the affected pool; p99 began to converge.

2026-02-19 09:00 UTC — RCA meeting: Hypothesis formed: tight coupling between backpressure admission signals and speculative kernel-probing logic caused feedback loop during burst admission, leading to repeated KV cache misses and path eviction.
2026-02-20 10:30 UTC — Postmortem created and initial action items drafted.
root_cause_summary: A race between the scheduler's admission/backpressure signals and the speculative kernel probing path selection resulted in frequent path re-evaluation at microbatch boundaries. Each re-evaluation triggered small kernel probes that evicted hot KV cache entries and created transient miss storms, which then fed back into the scheduler causing further probing — a positive feedback loop that amplified under surges.
analysis_notes: Telemetry: Correlated kernel-change events with KV cache miss-rate increases (2.3x baseline) and elevated microbatch GC cycles.
Repro: Synthetic burst load with 1.5–2x normal concurrency reproduced flapping locally with our 4x-A100 worker image when probe window <= 200ms.
Localization: Problem concentrated on mixed-quant model variants using fast-attn kernels with short sequence-length tails; homogeneous pools did not exhibit the same severity.
Why previous mitigations failed: Rapidly toggling the global probe rate mitigated symptoms but did not address sticky-score decay causing frequent re-ranking under load.
mitigation_summary: Short-term: disable speculative probing and raise probe damping threshold for affected pools; enable aggressive KV cache pinning for pinned model versions. Medium-term: implement capacity fence and a sticky-path scoring TTL; add probe jitter and admission hysteresis. Long-term: CI eval harness and a scheduler admission simulator to detect flapping regressions before rollout.
action_items: Ravi Singh - implement probe damping and jitter in scheduler: add randomized exponential backoff for per-route probes (ETA: 2026-03-05)
Jordan Lee - add sticky-path scoring TTL: keep winning path score for N seconds after assignment to prevent immediate re-ranking (ETA: 2026-03-12)
Priya Patel - implement capacity fence mechanism: reserve a small admission token pool during probe windows to prevent admission surges from triggering probes (ETA: 2026-03-18)
Carlos Mendes - KV cache pinning toggle: allow platform to pin KV keys for canaried models during rollout (ETA: 2026-03-08)
Ava Martinez - build synthetic surge eval harness and integrate into CI: load patterns that previously reproduced flapping; output SLO regression alerts (ETA: 2026-03-22)
Ravi Singh - ship runtime-1.19.3 hotfix that disables speculative probing by default and exposes a controlled flag (ETA: 2026-03-03)
All - telemetry tickets: create dashboards for probe-event correlation, KV miss storms, and microbatch churn (owner: Observability team, lead: Maya Chen) (ETA: 2026-03-01)
Security - confirm no sensitive data exposure in pinned cache metadata; provide sign-off (owner: Security team) (ETA: 2026-03-10)
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic surge eval harness reproduces previous flapping pattern in CI and shows reduction in p99 after changes
No regression in baseline throughput on unit/e2e tests (<=5% variance) after enabling probe damping
New dashboards show probe-events decoupled from KV miss-rate spikes for 7 days in canary pool
Capacity fence default configuration applied to Dedicated pools and validated under controlled load
